summary: Johannes Gildemeister (1812–1890) was an indologist and linguist. He studied at Göttingen under Heinrich Ewald and at Bonn under Georg Wilhelm Freytag and Christian Lassen. He was later a professor at Marburg (~1845–1859) and Bonn (~1859–1890).

Johannes Hertel (1872–1955) worked in Indology, earning his PhD from Leipzig University in 1897. He served as professor at Lessing-Gymnasium Döbeln (~1898–1920) and held the chair of Indian philology at Leipzig University (~1920–1937), succeeding Ernst Windisch.

Johannes Klatt (1852–1903) was an Indology scholar who studied under Albrecht Weber (~1869–1872) and at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1872–1873). From ~1874 to 1892, he served as custos of the Indian department at the Berlin State Library.

Johannes Nobel (1887–1960) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Heinrich Lüders and Genjun Sasaki. His academic career included posts at Humboldt University (~1920–1927) and Marburg (~1927–1955) as professor.

Johannes Rahder (1898–1988), an Indologist, Japanologist, and Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Utrecht University (~1920–1926). He held posts at Utrecht (1930–1931), Leiden (1931–1946; Chair of Japanese), the University of Hawaii (1946–1947), and Yale (1947–1965; Professor).

Johannes Schmidt (1843–1901) was a linguist and indologist who studied at Bonn, Jena under August Schleicher, and under Albrecht Weber. He held posts at Bonn (~1868–1873), Graz (~1873–1876), and Humboldt University of Berlin (professor in 1888).

Johannes Schneider (b. 1964) works in indology, tibetology, and buddhist studies. He has held a post at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1999) and served as an editorial board member for the Deshana Institute.

Johannes Schubert (1896–1976) was a scholar of tibetology and sinology. He studied under August Conrady and August Hermann Francke, held a post at Ahnenerbe (~1938–1945), and became professor of Tibetan at Leipzig University in 1960.

John A. Ardussi is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied under Turrell V. Wylie and earned his PhD from the Australian National University (~1972–1977), later serving as an ANU researcher and CNRS research team member (~2000).

John A. Brinkman (b. 1934) is a history and archaeology scholar. He held appointments at the University of Chicago and served as professor at the Institute for the Study of Ancient Cultures from ~1964 to 2005.

John Allan (1884–1955) worked in history, archaeology, and indology. He studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1903–1907) and Leipzig University (~1907–1908), and served as Keeper of the Department of Coins and Medals at the British Museum (~1931–1949).

John Avery (1837–1887) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Amherst College, under William Dwight Whitney, and at Berlin and Tübingen. He served as Professor of Greek at Grinnell College (1870–1877) and Bowdoin College (1877–1887).

John Borthwick Gilchrist (1759–1841) was a linguist and indologist educated at Edinburgh. He worked for the East India Company (~1782–1804) and held teaching posts at Fort William College (~1800–1804) and East India Company College (1806).

John Brough (1917–1984) was an indologist and linguist who studied at Edinburgh under Arthur Berriedale Keith and Cambridge under Harold Walter Bailey. He held posts at the British Museum, SOAS, University of London, and Cambridge (professor 1967–1984).
John Buescher is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his doctoral dissertation at the University of Virginia (~1977–1982) and later served as Director at Voice of America.

John Chadwick (1920–1998) was a scholar in linguistics, history, and archaeology. Educated at St Paul's School and Corpus Christi College, Cambridge (~1939–1946), he held an academic post at the University of Cambridge from ~1952 to 1984.
John Claude White (1853–1918) was active in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He received his education at Rugby School (~1867–1871) and the Royal Indian Engineering College (~1873–1876).

John Clifford Holt (b. 1948) works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Gustavus Adolphus College, Graduate Theological Union, and the University of Chicago under Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah. He held posts at Bowdoin College and Calgary.
John Collinson Nesfield (1836–1919) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He completed his education at Highgate School and Merton College (~1855–1860).

John Corrigan (b. 1952) works in religious studies and history/archaeology. After studying at the University of Chicago (~1976–1982), he held posts at Virginia, Harvard, Arizona State, and Florida State University, where he became Department of Religion Chair (~2001).
